title: Finite affine subring models of a marked gluing record
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme with a selected finite affine gluing presentation $\mathsf H$ [def-nagata-finite-affine-gluing-presentation]. All rings below are commutative with identity, including the zero ring. Retain the original charts and all the auxiliary affine opens, basic-open covers, restriction maps, comparisons and equations recorded in $\mathsf H$. Allow finitely many additional marked affine opens and finite basic-open refinements. Assign every additional affine open to a main chart containing it; if the main cover is empty, mark no additional affine opens. For every recorded inclusion of affine opens $P\subseteq Q$, fix a finite list $F_{PQ}\subseteq A_Q=\Gamma(Q,\mathcal O_X)$ with
$$P=\bigcup_{f\in F_{PQ}}D_Q(f),\qquad D_Q(f)\subseteq P.$$
For a recorded basic open $P=D_Q(f)$ retain the singleton list $\{f\}$. Include the restrictions of these elements among the marked elements of the smaller rings. A marked empty open is allowed and has ring zero; its cover may be empty. Finite covers of nonaffine overlap domains are retained as unions of the recorded affine or basic opens, not treated as single affine charts.

A *finite affine subring model of this finite record* is a tuple $B=(B_P)_P$, where $B_P\subseteq A_P$ is the subring generated by some finite subset together with the integers. Require the following properties of the tuple.

1. Every marked element of $A_P$ belongs to $B_P$. For each recorded inclusion $P\subseteq Q$, the actual restriction $\rho_{QP}:A_Q\to A_P$ sends $B_Q$ into $B_P$. Its restricted map is denoted $\rho^B_{QP}$. For every $f\in F_{PQ}$, restriction induces an isomorphism
$$B_Q[1/f]\longrightarrow B_P[1/\rho_{QP}(f)].$$
The elements $\rho_{QP}(f)$, $f\in F_{PQ}$, generate the unit ideal of $B_P$: there are $c_f\in B_P$ with $\sum_f c_f\rho_{QP}(f)=1$. Localizations and affine spectra have the meanings of [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Also require that the induced map $\operatorname{Spec}(B_P)\to\operatorname{Spec}(B_Q)$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] with image $\bigcup_{f\in F_{PQ}}D_{B_Q}(f)$.
2. Every other recorded localized comparison and its reverse sends the appropriate localized $B$-ring into the indicated localized $B$-ring, when both are mapped into their original localized $A$-rings. Its small map is that restriction, rather than an independently chosen homomorphism. The relevant localized $B$-ring is identified with its image in the localized $A$-ring. For a finite set of denominators, localization means successive localization at those elements, equivalently at their product.
3. Interpreting the entire finite record on $\operatorname{Spec}(B_P)$ and these induced maps, every marked finite covering is still a covering, every marked identification of overlap domains is still an identification, and the identity, inverse, open-preservation and triple-cocycle equations have exactly the domains and equalities displayed in $\mathsf H$. In particular the whole-overlap opens $W^B_{ab}$ satisfy $W^B_{aa}=\operatorname{Spec}(B_{U_a})$ and
$$
(\varphi^B_{ab})^{-1}(W^B_{ba}\cap W^B_{bc})=W^B_{ab}\cap W^B_{ac},\qquad
\varphi^B_{bc}\circ\varphi^B_{ab}=\varphi^B_{ac}\text{ on }W^B_{ab}\cap W^B_{ac}.
$$
Here whole-overlap opens and their maps are the unions of the marked basic-open pieces and their induced comparisons. All cover and equation requirements are properties, not additional ring or map data.

The underlying data of a model is only the finite tuple of actual subrings; the restriction and localization maps are determined by that tuple. Modelhood does not assert that any such tuple exists. A *finite seed* is a family of finite subsets $E_P\subseteq A_P$; a model contains it if $E_P\subseteq B_P$ for every marked affine $P$. For models of the same record, $B\leq C$ means $B_P\subseteq C_P$ for every $P$.
